_comment: Shipped defaults, and the documentation of everything you can set. Do NOT edit this file — run `npm run setup`, which writes config.json next to it. config.json wins key by key; anything it leaves out falls back to here.
title: Agent Console
_bindHost: 127.0.0.1 keeps it on this machine only. Setup writes 0.0.0.0 if you said you would open it from somewhere else.
_allowedHostNames: Extra hostnames you will type in the browser. localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] are always allowed. Anything else is refused, which is what stops another site from driving this one.
_workRoots: The ONLY folders a terminal may be started in. A requested folder is resolved for real, so `..` and a symlink out are the same refusal. This app's own scratch folder (~/.agent-console/work) is always added.
_harnesses: The coding CLIs a tile can run. `bin` is looked up on your PATH (or give an absolute path). Nothing here is ever executed to probe it — a missing CLI just shows as NOT INSTALLED until you install it. `home`: omit for your own HOME, or "private" for a seeded HOME of its own, or an absolute path. `install` is the vendor's own install command; `npm run setup` prints it for the CLIs you don't have and offers to run them.

cursor.name: CURSOR
cursor.label: Cursor Agent
cursor._bin: Cursor's installer names the executable `agent` and puts it in ~/.local/bin — which is the default `pathPrefix`, so a tile finds it. `agent` is a generic name: another program called that, earlier on your PATH, is what would be launched. Nothing is ever executed to probe it, so the only test is that the file is executable. Set an absolute path here if that worries you.

_agents: Named tiles that always run the same CLI in the same folder. None ship. Each is { id, name, role, harness, cwd, icon, accent }. `icon` is one of dot, ring, bar, grok. `accent: true` paints one agent orange — at most one. Add `telegram: { tokenEnv: "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_X" }` to give it a bot; the token itself lives in .env.
_pathPrefix: Prepended to PATH for every terminal, so a CLI in ~/.local/bin is found even when the server was started by systemd with a minimal PATH. Defaults to ~/.local/bin, which is where the cursor and grok installers put their binaries.
_scrubEnv: Environment variables to strip from every terminal. Put your own secrets here — a coding CLI is a place where `env` is one keystroke.
_dropPrivileges: Linux and root only: run a terminal as the owner of its folder via setpriv. Off by default; it does not exist on macOS.
_optional: These three mirror an existing Claude Code setup into the private HOME, and only apply to a harness with "home": "private". null = skip, which is the default.
